advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the bot's retrigger reply messages provably inert (remove the literal `recheck-review` token from reply text or add an independent recursion/rate guard) so the author-based loop guard is not the sole defense against a self-trigger loop.
evidence: retrigger.py:134 `_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE = ("recheck-review accepted: ..."` — reply text contains the trigger token
retrigger.py:126 `"recheck-review refused: this revision's LLM-Review -1 is a REAL FINDING "` — refusal text also contains the token

retrigger.py:160-161 `if author == cfg.bot_user: return None  # loop guard` — the only guard; `author = str(((event.get("author") or {}).get("username")) or "")` yields "" if the field is absent/renamed, which will not equal a non-empty bot_user

ABSENCE: the reply messages are not made token-free, and there is no independent rate/recursion cap, so a single loop-guard miss (field-shape drift or bot_user mismatch) causes an unbounded reply loop
advisory.finding: The bot's own reply messages (`_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE` and `_refusal_message`) both begin with the literal `recheck-review` token, so the author-based loop guard is the SOLE protection against an infinite self-trigger loop. If a `comment-added` event ever omits/renames `author.username`, or `bot_user` is misconfigured, the bot's reply re-arrives, re-matches `_TOKEN_RE`, and re-triggers indefinitely (accepted path also re-posts + re-enqueues each cycle).
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword `_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE`/`_refusal_message` so they do not contain the bare `recheck-review` token (e.g. phrase as "re-review accepted…"/backtick-escape differently), keeping the author loop guard as defense-in-depth rather than the only line.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with RetriggerGerrit(change_exists=False) asserting handle_comment_added returns None, posts no reply, and emits RETRIGGER_REFUSED reason=change-not-found.
evidence: retrigger.py:178-187 `fresh = gc.get_change_event(...)` / `if fresh is None:` -> `_emit(... reason="change-not-found")` / `return None`
RetriggerGerrit defines the affordance: tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py:60 `def __init__(self, ... change_exists: bool = True)` and :68 `if not self.change_exists: return None`
search_files for `change_exists` in the test file returned no matches beyond the double's own definition — the False path is never driven
ABSENCE: a regression that dropped the None-guard would crash on `fresh["change"]["id"]` (NoneType subscript) on a deleted/inaccessible change and no test would catch it
advisory.finding: The change-not-found branch (get_change_event returns None -> emits RETRIGGER_REFUSED with reason=change-not-found and returns None without posting a reply) is untested. The test double RetriggerGerrit even defines a `change_exists` flag purpose-built for this path, but no test ever constructs it with change_exists=False.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_change_not_found_is_refused_without_reply(tmp_path, caplog)` using `RetriggerGerrit(change_exists=False)`; assert result is None, gerrit.comments == [], and 'change-not-found' / 'RETRIGGER_REFUSED' in caplog.text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting _comment_event(project='other') is a no-op (returns None, no lookups, no comments) when cfg.project='rebar'.
evidence: retrigger.py:166-169 `project = change.get("project")` / `if cfg.project and project and project != cfg.project: return None`
tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py:37 `_comment_event(..., project: str = "rebar")` — parameter exists but is never overridden
search_files for `project` in the test file returned no matches (only the default in the helper), so no test drives a mismatch
ABSENCE: a regression deleting/weakening the project guard would let recheck-review on a non-configured project trigger a re-review, and no test would fail
advisory.finding: The project guard (`if cfg.project and project and project != cfg.project: return None`) is untested. The _comment_event helper exposes a `project` parameter but no test passes a project that mismatches cfg.project, so a comment on a foreign project is never verified to be a no-op.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_foreign_project_is_a_noop(tmp_path)` calling handle_comment_added with `_comment_event(project="other")`; assert result is None and gerrit.lookups == [] and gerrit.comments == [].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where post_comment raises GerritError, asserting the accepted path still returns the forced event (and the refusal path still returns None) without propagating.
evidence: retrigger.py:225-228 accept path: `try: gc.post_comment(...) except GerritError: logger.warning(...)` then `return fresh`
retrigger.py:203-207 refuse path: same swallow before `return None`
docstring retrigger.py:153-154 states the contract: 'Replies are best-effort — a failed reply must not lose the accepted re-review or crash the worker.'
ABSENCE: RetriggerGerrit.post_comment (test file :79) always returns 200; no variant raises GerritError, so the swallow branch is never executed
advisory.finding: The best-effort reply-failure contract is untested. Both the acceptance and refusal paths wrap `gc.post_comment(...)` in try/except GerritError explicitly so a failed reply 'must not lose the accepted re-review or crash the worker' (docstring), but no test injects a post_comment that raises to prove the accepted forced event is still returned (and the refusal still returns None) when the reply fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Give RetriggerGerrit an optional `raise_on_comment=True` (or subclass) whose post_comment raises GerritError; assert an eligible state still returns a `_rebar_force` event and the budget was reset, and a finding state still returns None.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden the retrigger loop guard against a bot reply re-triggering: cross-check the bot identity on more than `author.username` alone (e.g. also `author.email`/account id) and/or refuse to act on any `comment-added` whose message is one of the bot's own reply templates, so a missing `username` field cannot open a self-amplifying accept→reply→re-trigger loop.
evidence: retrigger.py:159-161: `author = str(((event.get("author") or {}).get("username")) or "")` then `if author == cfg.bot_user: return None  # loop guard`
retrigger.py:134-138: `_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE = ("recheck-review accepted: ...")` — the bot's own reply contains the whole-word trigger token that `_TOKEN_RE` (retrigger.py:49) matches

gerrit_client.py post_comment (diff): `body = {"message": message}` — deliberately NO tag, so the bot's reply comments carry no `autogenerated:rebar` marker that a secondary loop guard could key on (unlike post_vote, gerrit_client.py:272 `"tag": "autogenerated:rebar"`)

ticket bb9b design note: 'Loop guard: ignore comments authored by the bot itself (cfg.bot_user), else the bot's own replies re-trigger events forever' — establishes this as a security-relevant invariant

ABSENCE: the accepted path (retrigger.py:209-229) re-arms the budget via reset_attempts and returns a forced event every time it runs, with no idempotency/dedup on the reply itself, so a fail-open loop guard is self-sustaining
advisory.finding: The self-trigger loop guard in `handle_comment_added` relies on a single event field (`author.username`) with no fallback and no secondary tag-based check; because the bot's own accepted/refusal replies contain the whole-word `recheck-review` token and are posted via `post_comment` with NO `autogenerated:rebar` tag, any `comment-added` event that does not populate `author.username` with the bot user (e.g. Gerrit shapes carrying only `author.name`/`email`) would let a bot reply re-trigger, producing a self-amplifying accept→reply→re-trigger loop that repeatedly re-arms the retry budget and force-re-reviews.
